M1-1.1.motivate: A real car has size, a rope stretches a little, and a wheel has friction. A useful mechanics model keeps the properties that affect the question. Which of these details can you ignore in a particular calculation?

discover.stem: A light inextensible string passes over a smooth pulley. Which conclusion follows from the model?

options.A: The string has no tension because it is light.
options.B: The taut string keeps a constant length and can carry tension.
options.C: The string cannot move because it is inextensible.
options.D: The pulley cannot exert any contact force because it is smooth.

discover.explanation: Light means negligible string mass, while inextensible means constant length when taut. Smooth removes friction at contact, not tension or the contact force.

M1-1.1.establish: A particle has mass but negligible dimensions. A lamina is a flat sheet of negligible thickness. A rigid body does not change shape or size under the forces considered. A light rod or string has negligible mass; light does not mean unable to transmit force. A uniform rod has mass evenly distributed along its length and, in uniform gravity, its centre of mass is at the midpoint. A non-uniform rod has uneven mass distribution. An inextensible string keeps a constant length when taut, so connected particles have linked displacements. A smooth surface has no friction but can exert a normal reaction; a rough surface may exert friction. A light smooth pulley has negligible mass and no friction at the string contact; with a light string, tension is equal on both sides. A bead is a small object constrained to move along a wire. A wire defines its path; a peg is a fixed small support around which a string can pass. A peg or wire needs a stated smoothness assumption before friction is ignored.
M1-1.1.connect: In a later connected-particle problem, first use inextensibility to link motion, then use the light string and smooth pulley to link tensions. For a rod in a moments problem, uniformity determines where its weight acts; rigidity only tells you its shape stays fixed.
M1-1.1.note:
- Particle: mass retained, size negligible; lamina: negligible thickness; rigid body: no deformation.
- Light: negligible mass; uniform: evenly distributed mass; non-uniform: uneven mass distribution.
- Inextensible: constant taut length; smooth: no friction; rough: friction may act.
- Light smooth pulley with light string: equal tensions on both sides.
- Bead: small object constrained to a wire; peg: fixed support for a string.
M1-1.1.self_explain: A uniform rod rests on a smooth table. Which assumption places its weight at the midpoint, and which removes friction? Explain why the table can still exert a normal reaction.
